subject: Distributional assumption done by lavaan when estimating two factors?

messages.author: e5c4db1a1cffab6b
messages.subject: Distributional assumption done by lavaan when estimating two factors?
parts:
Hello 

I am wondering what assumption lavaan does about the distribution of the latent factors when estimating them. 

Does it assume joint normality or a mixture of normal distribution of the two factors?

In order to be more concrete, let me please provide you with this example:

model <- '
# 1st factor
#loadings
F1=~    1*x1 +  x2 +   x3  
# threshold
x1          | 0*t1 + t2
x2          | t1 + t2
x3          | t1 + t2
# mean and std of factor
F1   ~~ NA* F1
F1  ~ NA*1

#2nd factor
#loadings
F2=~    1*x4 +  x5 +   x6  
# threshold
x4          | 0*t1 + t2
x5          | t1 + t2
x6          | t1 + t2
# mean and std of factor
F2   ~~ NA* F2
F2  ~ NA*1
'
sem <- sem(model , data=my_data, std.lv=F, estimator="dwls",parameterization="theta")

Many thanks
Dea

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Distributional assumption done by lavaan when estimating two factors?
parts: I am wondering what assumption lavaan does about the distribution of the latent factors when estimating them

Common and unique factors are assumed multivariate normal, as are latent item responses underlying observed ordinal responses.

When all outcomes are continuous, you can relax the normality assumption by requesting robust SEs and tests (see ?lavOptions help page for description of options se= and test=, where estimator= can be used as a shortcut for both).  No such relaxation is possible for ordered= outcomes, which would require much more flexibility in specifying likelihoods from different distributions to test the best fit.  Here is an article with examples of comparing a few distributions using R's nlminb() optimizer:

https://doi.org/10.3390/psych3040037
